LESSON: POSITION AND SIZE OF COUNTRIES IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: NATURAL AND THE BUILT ENVIRONMENTS Strand Sub- Strand Specific Learning Outcomes
Topic 1.1: Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa, part of NATURAL AND THE BUILT ENVIRONMENTS Strand Sub- Strand Specific Learning Outcomes in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade six SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: How would we describe the position of countries in Eastern Africa? 2. How do we locate places on a map?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Position and Size of Countries in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
• Patriotism: learners realize their sense of loyalty, social and moral/signed duties as they sing/sign sing the East African Community

Anthem.

• Respect: learners appreciate diverse opinions as they brainstorm in groups on the difference between latitudes and longitudes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

• Critical Thinking: learners build their critical thinking skills as they brainstorm in groups on the difference between latitudes and

longitudes.

• Citizenship: learners demonstrate patriotism as they sing/sign-sing the East African Community Anthem.

Link to other learning areas:

● Science and technology: learners play computer games on latitudes and longitudes.

● Creative Arts: Learners apply skills learnt in creative arts as they draw latitudes and longitudes on a sketch map of Eastern Africa.
